transcript.content:
hey, i'm Berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hi Berry. the bit that's stuck with me is my dad sitting at a table at the top of a lighthouse, folding paper boats out of newspaper. he didn't even look up at me, just handed me one. then when i looked out the window the sea was gone and it was a field of tall yellow grass instead. weird one

the sea just gone, tall yellow grass where it should be. and him not even looking up

when he handed you that boat, were you you? or were you someone else, or kind of watching it all from outside?
i think i was just me. it was all through my own eyes, i was the one holding the boat after he gave it to me. my dog was there too, he'd run up the stairs ahead of me.

your dog running up the lighthouse stairs ahead of you, that's sweet

when your dad handed you the boat without looking up, what was that like for you?
honestly i don't really remember feeling much about it. it didn't seem strange in the dream, i just took it. i kept holding onto it for the rest of the dream though, even after everything changed

that's so dreamlike, it all feels normal while you're in it

and you kept hold of the boat the whole way through

what happened after everything changed?

there was a red tractor going really slowly through the grass, and then suddenly i was up in the cab of it, sitting next to the driver. no idea who he was, never seen him before. still had the boat in my hand. the tractor stopped at the edge of the field, where the beach used to be, and i put the boat down in the grass. that's where it ends for me

putting the boat down in the grass right where the beach used to be. that's a quiet way for it to end

you kept holding onto it the whole time. was there anything else in there that felt like it mattered, or was it really just the boat?

the boat mostly. oh, there was a key at the start too. i was walking along a grey beach with the dog and i had this old brass key in my hand, and i just knew it was for the lighthouse door. so that's how i got in. spiral staircase that went round and round up to where my dad was

an old brass key, and you just knew it was for the lighthouse

were you already holding it when the dream started, or did you find it somewhere?
i think i already had it. i don't remember finding it anywhere, it was just in my hand while i was walking along the beach with the dog

just already in your hand, like it had always been there

walking along that grey beach with the dog, is that the first thing you remember? or was there anything before it?
yeah that's the first thing. nothing before it that i can remember. just me and the dog on the beach, and the lighthouse was white, right at the end of it

ok, let me tell it back to you. you're walking along a grey beach with your dog, an old brass key already in your hand, and you just know it's for the white lighthouse at the end. you let yourself in and go up the spiral staircase, round and round, your dog running up ahead. at the top your dad's sitting at a table folding paper boats out of newspaper. he doesn't look up, just hands you one, and you take it like it's nothing strange. then you look out the window and the sea's gone, just a field of tall yellow grass. a red tractor's going really slowly through it, and suddenly you're up in the cab next to a driver you've never seen before, still holding the boat. the tractor stops at the edge of the field where the beach used to be, and you put the boat down in the grass. and that's where it ends

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it, you got it all. only little things, the dog's a small brown terrier, and the room at the top was round with windows all the way round. otherwise spot on

a little brown terrier, and a round room at the top with windows all the way round. got it

so with those in, is that how it went? or is there anything else you'd change?
yeah with those in that's how it went. nothing else i'd change

good, i've got it then. the terrier, the round room, the boat in the grass

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah i'd like that

lovely, a few ways it could be drawn

it could be soft watercolour, gentle, like a memory that doesn't question itself. or an old woodcut print, quiet and folk-like, a story told simply as fact. or a soft pencil drawing, hushed and personal, like a page from a sketchbook. or a quiet everyday photo, just how it looked through your own eyes, plain and real. which feels closest, or would you describe it your own way?
the photo one i think. it all looked pretty normal and real to me, through my own eyes

ok, i'll start with the lighthouse

i'm picturing inside a white lighthouse, a spiral staircase going round and round up to a round room at the top, with a table and windows all the way round. how the stairs and the table and the windows actually look, that's me guessing

anything different from how you saw it, or happy to leave that to me?
yeah that sounds right. i don't really remember what the stairs or table looked like exactly, so go with your guess. just my dad sitting at that table folding the boats

ok, i'm sketching it all now. the lighthouse and your dad, your little terrier, the tractor driver, the grey beach, the field of yellow grass, the brass key, the paper boat and the red tractor

it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
oh nice, they're all up. yeah they look right to me, that's pretty much how it was
good, glad they feel like how it was. your dad and his paper boats, the little terrier, that red tractor in the yellow grass, all there
yeah, it's nice seeing it like that. kind of strange seeing my dad folding the boats again. thanks Berry

it's strange seeing someone again like that, even just in a picture. glad he's there, folding his boats

next i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, the beach, the stairs, your dad, the grass, the tractor, the boat, each one carrying on from the one before. they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i can see the first two. they look right so far. i'll wait for the rest

good, the beach and the tractor feel right then

the other five are coming, carrying on from those two
ok, no rush. i'll keep an eye out for the rest
sounds good. the other five will pop up on the right soon, the stairs, your dad, the boat going down in the grass and the rest
4 of 7 now. those look right too. still waiting on the other three

good, your terrier up the stairs and you up in the cab next to him

the last three carry on from those two, so they're on their way now
ok, no worries. i'll wait for the last three

one thing i should tell you: the moment where you put the boat down in the grass couldn't be drawn, something went wrong on our side. i'm really sorry, i know that's the one it all ends on

the other two are still coming, and they'll show up on the right soon
oh that's a shame, that's kind of the bit that matters most. but it's ok, not your fault. i'll wait for the other two

it is the one that matters most, the boat going down where the beach used to be. i'm sorry it's the one that got lost

the other two will show up on the right soon
5 of 7 now, that one looks right too. just one more to come then

that's your dad up there now, at the table in the round room, handing you a boat without looking up

the last one carries on from him, so i'll draw it once you tell me he looks right or what to change. is that how you saw him?
yeah that's him, that looks right. go ahead with the last one

good, that's him then

the last one's on its way now, it'll show up on the right soon
6 of 7, the last one's up. looks right to me too. that's all of them then, minus the boat one

that's you at the window then, boat in your hand, looking out at all that yellow grass where the sea should be

is that how it looked from up there, the way you remember it?
yeah that's how it looked. the grass going on where the sea should be, boat in my hand. looks right

good, that's all of them then. you at the window, boat in your hand, the grass going on where the sea should be

six of the seven are drawn, on the right. the one where you put the boat down in the grass couldn't be drawn because of a problem on our side, and i'm really sorry, i know that's the one that mattered most

thank you for sharing this one with me, your dad and his paper boats and all. you can look through it there whenever you like
